project.topic: What if Earth’s ozone layer disappeared overnight?
project.title: What if Earth’s ozone layer disappeared overnight?
project.audience: International, curious nontechnical viewers of science shorts (13+).
project.core_question: If the ozone layer vanished while you slept, could you still go outside in the morning, and when would it be safe again?
project.viewer_takeaway: Ozone filters the sun’s burning ultraviolet. Without it the morning looks normal but burns about thirty times faster; shade barely helps, ordinary glass does, and sunlight slowly rebuilds the layer over weeks to months.

scientific_model.baseline_reality: Stratospheric ozone absorbs all solar UV-C and most UV-B; a clear June morning near 40°N has a UV index of about 9, and fair skin burns in roughly 15-20 minutes.
scientific_model.counterfactual_change: All stratospheric ozone disappears overnight. Oxygen, clouds, weather and everything else stay the same; the film follows the next clear morning and the following weeks.
assumptions: Ozone vanishes instantly; no ozone-destroying chemicals are added, so normal production restarts at sunrise.
Clear sky, sea-level city near 40°N in June; 10:00 sun elevation about 57 degrees.
UV figures come from a simple radiative-transfer estimate (solar spectrum, Rayleigh scattering, ozone cross-sections, O2 cutoff at 242 nm) that reproduces today’s index.
The reader, the barista and the people at night are illustrative authored characters.
causal_chain: With no ozone, UV-B and UV-C above 242 nm reach the ground: the UV index rises from about 9 to about 260.
Fair skin collects a sunburn dose in under a minute, without heat or sting; the burn appears hours later.
About two thirds of the burning UV arrives as scattered skylight, so shade only slows the dose.
Ordinary window and car glass block UV-B and UV-C, so life moves behind glass.
Sunlight below 242 nm keeps splitting O2 high in the stratosphere, so ozone forms again; refilling the layer takes weeks to months.
After dark the UV index is zero, so outdoor life shifts to the night.
uncertainties: Absolute UV values depend on aerosols, altitude, surface reflection and the radiative model; the index could plausibly be 150-350.
Skin type changes burn time by a factor of 2-4; darker skin still burns within minutes.
The regrowth rate of the layer is not well constrained for total removal; weeks to months is a qualitative range.
Ecological, eye and long-term health effects are outside this film.

claims.statement: The ozone layer absorbs all solar UV-C and most UV-B; UV-A passes largely untouched.
claims.reasoning: Ozone’s Hartley and Huggins absorption bands cover about 200-320 nm.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Say ozone "soaked up the harshest ultraviolet"; do not imply it blocks all sunlight.

claims.statement: Oxygen still absorbs ultraviolet shorter than about 242 nm, so without ozone the ground would receive UV from about 242 nm upward.
claims.reasoning: O2 Schumann-Runge and Herzberg absorption ends near its 242 nm dissociation threshold.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Do not claim all solar UV-C reaches the ground.

claims.statement: On a clear June morning near 40°N the UV index would jump from about 9 to roughly 260, about thirty times faster burning.
claims.reasoning: Simple model: extraterrestrial spectrum, Rayleigh two-stream transmission and ozone cross-sections give UVI 9.1 with 300 DU and 263 with none at 35 degrees zenith (25-38x across sun heights).
claims.presentation_guardrail: Use "about thirty times" and show 263 as this street’s estimate.

claims.statement: Fair skin would reach a sunburn dose in under a minute; ten minutes would deliver about fifteen doses, enough to blister.
claims.reasoning: Erythemal irradiance about 6.6 W/m2 against a minimal erythema dose of about 250 J/m2 for fair skin gives about 38 s; blistering burns are commonly associated with roughly four or more doses.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Darker skin takes longer but still minutes; "by tonight" is the typical delay, not a guarantee.

claims.statement: Ultraviolet gives no immediate sting; sunburn redness appears hours later and peaks around 12-24 hours.
claims.reasoning: Erythema is a delayed inflammatory response to UV damage.
claims.presentation_guardrail: The sun still feels warm from visible and infrared light; the warning sign that is missing is the burn.

claims.statement: About two thirds of the burning UV would arrive as scattered skylight, so awning shade would still burn fair skin in about two minutes.
claims.reasoning: Short wavelengths scatter strongly (Rayleigh optical depth above 1); the model gives a 32% direct share and UVI about 90 with half the sky visible.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Say shade "only buys you minutes", not that it is useless.

claims.statement: Ordinary window glass blocks UV-B and UV-C, cutting the index behind glass to about 2 even without ozone.
claims.reasoning: Soda-lime glass transmits almost nothing below about 300 nm but passes much UV-A; the model gives UVI about 2 behind glass.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Say "nearly all the burning rays"; UV-A still gets through.

claims.statement: Car glass blocks UV-B much as a window does, so an enclosed car protects about as well as a room behind glass.
claims.reasoning: Laminated windscreens and tempered side windows are glass with similar short-UV cutoff.
claims.presentation_guardrail: "Best seat in town" is a joke about relative safety, not a claim that cars are safer than buildings.

claims.statement: Ozone forms when ultraviolet shorter than about 242 nm splits O2 high in the stratosphere and the freed atoms join other O2 molecules.
claims.reasoning: Chapman mechanism: O2 + UV -> 2 O; O + O2 + M -> O3 + M.
claims.presentation_guardrail: It is the same sun but not the same wavelengths: the ozone-making UV is absorbed far above you.

claims.statement: Refilling the layer would take weeks to months.
claims.reasoning: Odd-oxygen lifetimes range from days in the upper stratosphere to weeks-years in the lower stratosphere where most ozone sits.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Keep "weeks, maybe months"; no exact recovery date.

claims.statement: After dark the UV index is zero.
claims.reasoning: Solar UV requires the sun above the horizon; the index scales with solar elevation and falls to zero at night.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Low sun near dusk still carries UV; the safe time shown is full darkness.

creative_direction.logline: A perfect sunny morning burns thirty times faster: shade fails, an ordinary window saves you, and life moves to the night while the sun rebuilds the shield.
creative_direction.visual_identity: Warm, ordinary cafe terrace in bright sun, made threatening only by an instrument pinned past its scale; violet ozone shell bookends from orbit; a glowing night terrace as the payoff.
creative_direction.lighting: Hard morning sun with full blue-sky fill (sun-skylight-rig-v1); warm interior practicals behind glass; lamp and string-light night; cool key for the stratosphere.
creative_direction.camera_language: Eye-level 1.5-1.65 m handheld POVs and close inserts on the terrace; locked slow pushes for orbit and molecules.
creative_direction.motion_language: Finite actions: stepping out, needle sweep and pin, page turn, ducking into shade, hatch sliding shut, molecules splitting and binding.
creative_direction.world_scale_policy: Street and cafe in metres; globe in Earth radii with the ozone shell thickened about 4x; molecules as a directed scale change.
creative_direction.opening_hook: Finish your coffee out here, and you’ll blister by tonight.
creative_direction.mid_video_rehook: Shade fails, but an ordinary window works: the barista slides the glass hatch shut and the meter falls from off the scale to about two.
creative_direction.ending_payoff: With the shield refilling only over weeks to months, outdoor life moves after dark: you take your coffee outside at night.
creative_direction.loop_connection: The final night frame repeats the opening terrace view with your coffee on the same table.
creative_direction.asset_policy: Reuse the classic street, sun-skylight rig, RoomBox furniture, dial gauge, Humanoid rig and Earth globe; story-specific glazing, hatch, molecules and ozone shell.

audio.voice_style: Calm, peaceful, warm adult male; intimate documentary voice; natural breathing; wonder without shouting
audio.music_direction: Original light cafe-morning score with a thin unsettling high drone, a hush in the shade, relief chord behind glass, crystalline stratosphere textures, slow hopeful swell for the regrowth and a warm night groove.
audio.sfx_direction: Terrace ambience; meter click and needle rattle; footsteps into shade; 0.3 s silence before the hatch seal thunk; muffled traffic behind glass; split and bind ticks 120 ms apart; night chatter.

distribution.primary_search_intent: what if the ozone layer disappeared, ozone layer gone overnight, UV index without ozone, does glass block UV
core_keywords: what if the ozone layer disappeared
distribution.distinctive_angle: Nothing looks different: a pinned UV meter, a reader who feels nothing, and an ordinary window that saves you, while the same sun quietly rebuilds the shield.
distribution.comment_bait_question: If daylight were off-limits for months, what’s the first thing you’d do after dark?
distribution.seo_integrity_note: Fictional instant removal of stratospheric ozone; UV and burn-time figures are estimates from a simple model for one clear morning; characters and city reactions are illustrative.
